steps.title: Eligibility and lock
in: The ticket, with its scope and dependencies
The ticket's criteria: those of the story's entries (or the subset the task carries), or those a technical ticket carries itself
out: Criteria ready (or in gap for a correction ticket), ADRs accepted, dependencies merged, no other open ticket on these criteria. A dependency whose Recette is in gap marks this ticket "on dependency in gap"
Taken by this agent, status in build
Functional ticket: its criteria, in their entries, at status in build

steps.title: Implementer
steps.actor: AI, in TDD: its tests first, then the code
in: Guidelines whose scope overlaps the ticket's. Selected by script
Technical-frame rules whose scope overlaps the ticket's
The project's test conventions, and current code
out: Its tests, written first from the criteria
Change within the ticket's scope, after its tests
Only if a choice is covered by nothing: see the next step

steps.title: Routed question
steps.actor: Human F or T, only if a choice is covered by nothing, or after two failures in a row
in: Card: options, effect, cost, recommendation. After two failures: the list of failing checks
out: Answer, recorded in the wiki or an ADR. Implementation resumes
Or impossible criterion: entry to reframe (Need workflow), or back to design for a technical ticket

steps.title: Validator
steps.actor: Persona distinct from the lead: it receives the deliverable alone, never the discussion
in: Guidelines whose scope overlaps the ticket's
out: List of defects, free critique: gap with an ADR or a guideline, readability, duplication, uncovered edge case

steps.title: Code checks
in: Technical-frame rules applicable to the ticket's scope
out: Tests green, run locally by the script before any PR, frame rules green, diff within the ticket's declared scope, hypotheses declared, each criterion referenced by at least one test of the diff (excluding e2e)
Status: in review, set when the checks pass

steps.title: Judge
steps.actor: AI, three fixed questions, citation required

questions.q: Does the change add behavior outside the criteria?
Does each test express its criterion, no more, no less?

out: Yes or no: does the change add behavior outside the criteria? is a hypothesis undeclared? does each test express its criterion, no more, no less?

steps.title: Code review
steps.actor: Reviewers of other types, in parallel, without seeing the implementer's reasoning or the others' opinions

agents.when: structure, performance, security: scope touching an ADR, a guideline, non-functional requirements, or technical ticket

in: Guidelines whose scope overlaps the ticket's
The ticket's type and scope, from which a script derives the list of reviewers
out: One opinion per reviewer on the diff: approves, or requests changes with its blocking defects, each classed "code", "test" or "criterion". Non-blocking defects are plain comments, recorded on the ticket

steps.title: Review decision
out: All opinions approve: the diff is approved

At least one opinion requests changes: routed by defect class. Code: back to the implementer, and the whole chain replays. Test: back to the implementer, who fixes their tests. Impossible or ambiguous criterion: question to human F, entry to reframe.

steps.title: e2e tests
steps.actor: AI, on the integrated behavior, once the diff is approved
in: Diff approved by the review, run locally by the script, never in CI
out: One e2e test per criterion "verified by e2e", added to the diff
A red test is classed by the agent: code defect (back to the implementer, and the whole chain replays) or test defect (it fixes it)

steps.title: Code checks
out: Each criterion "verified by e2e" has an e2e test attached, all GREEN, run locally by the script

steps.title: Judge

questions.q: Does each e2e test express its criterion, no more, no less?

out: Yes or no: does each e2e test express its criterion, no more, no less?

steps.title: PR opening and CI
in: Diff approved by the review, e2e green
Code checks and judge, all green
out: Pull request opened on the ticket's branch: the diff, the ticket link and the reports in the description. It only serves to get the CI to run, without the e2e
CI green on the PR: the script waits for the result

steps.title: Merge on main
out: PR merged on main by the script, after the green CI
Status: "merged, awaiting Recette" for an unsplit story, "merged" for a task. When all its tasks are merged, the story moves to "merged, awaiting Recette", by script
Functional ticket: its criteria at status implemented, with the commit. Technical ticket: criteria set to status implemented
Declared hypotheses, recorded on the ticket for the Recette

contract: A ticket at status ready: an unsplit story or a task, created by Plan, or by the Recette for a correction. It references criteria, ADRs, a scope and its dependencies.

Code merged on main, the ticket at status "merged, awaiting Recette" (a task: "merged") and its criteria at status implemented, with the commit. A split story moves to "merged, awaiting Recette" when all its tasks are merged, by script.
No human required. Human F or T only answers a question.
notes: No human gate
The merge is controlled by the code checks, the judge, the code review, the e2e tests and the CI. The human validates the behavior afterwards, in the Recette.
Two marks, two verifications
"Implemented" is set here by code: the test written for the criterion passes. "Recetted" is only set by the Recette.
After two failures
The ticket is blocked and a question goes to the human concerned. There is no gate left to open it.
No technical plan here
Decisions come from technical design. This avoids a stale plan when the ticket waits.
Who reviews the diff

A script derives the reviewers from the ticket's type and scope, among the existing personas. The tech lead already validated the implementation at step 4 and does not review a second time. The PM reviews a functional ticket: are the criteria met. The architect reviews structure, performance and security when the scope touches them, or if the ticket is technical. The designer reviews usage and accessibility of an interface scope. Each reads the guidelines and frame rules relevant to their angle: there is no separate checklist.
The PR comes last

The review covers the local diff, before any PR. The PR is opened only once the review, the e2e and all checks have passed: it only serves to get the CI to run. Every review round trip therefore happens locally, without consuming GitHub quota.
Where a change request goes

As close to the cause as possible. A code defect goes back to the implementer, already validated tests stay. A test defect goes back to the implementer, who fixes their tests. An impossible or ambiguous criterion goes to human F. The defect class is set by the reviewer, the routing by a script.
Tests stay
The dev's tests and the e2e tests are merged with the code. The dev's remain regression tests, replayed by the CI. The e2e are not replayed by the CI: a script runs them locally, on demand.
e2e tests at the end

The dev works in TDD: tests come before the code, so e2e tests before the code would add nothing. They are written at the end, on the integrated behavior, once the diff is approved, and only for criteria whose verified-by is e2e. They never run in CI, as they consume too much GitHub quota: a script runs them locally.
Recette on the complete story
The Recette covers a story whose tasks are all merged, never a single task.
Hypotheses
A technical choice not covered by a decision is not a hypothesis: it is a question, at the dedicated step. Other hypotheses are declared and seen at the Recette.
A validator

It replaces human code reading, which has no value. It looks for what neither the tests nor the rules see: a gap with an ADR, readability, an edge case. The tests the dev writes first remain the main control.
A technical ticket
Its criteria are technical (non-regression, invariant). Its Recette is held by human T.
doc.lede: A ticket becomes code merged on main, verified by the tests the dev writes first (TDD), then by e2e tests just before the merge. No human intervenes, except for a question. Behavior is validated afterwards, by the Recette.
